A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same authors' CSBO-to-SBO reduction framework. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 Section 6 reports original data-cleaning experiments with 30% label corruption, including convergence curves and temperature-specific validation-loss analyses in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 Section 5 reports original MNIST hyperparameter-optimization and synthetic traffic inverse-optimization results. Appendix A documents the experiments and repeated trials.

M1.justification: Both versions approximate context-dependent lower-level solutions by W times a feature map, optimize the resulting joint-expectation SBO problem, and use existing SBO solvers. The additional monomial and Fourier evaluations instantiate the existing framework; they do not introduce a new optimization procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains temperature-dependent data cleaning, now explicitly identified as MNIST, and adds inverse capacity estimation on a synthetic two-edge traffic network. Recovering capacities from demand and noisy equilibrium-flow observations substantially extends the evaluated tasks and domains.

E2.justification: v1 Figure 2 compares against stocBio, DL-SGD, and RT-SGD. v2 retains stocBiO as its external comparator but removes the direct DL-SGD/RT-SGD comparisons. Appendix A explains exclusion of DL-SGD and the randomized scheme it calls RT-MLMC. This materially narrows comparison against existing CSBO methods.

E3.justification: Hyperparameter evaluation changes from validation loss against runtime to training and validation losses against epochs; plotted stocBiO sizes change from 1, 5, 10 to 5, 10, 20, 50. The new inverse experiment introduces separate 1,000-sample training/test sets, averaging over the last 10% of epochs, exact lower-level solutions for testing, and parameter/solution-error metrics.

E4.justification: v1's temperature-specific heatmaps and analysis of lower-level coverage disappear. v2 adds systematic comparisons of basis families and basis sizes, examining approximation saturation, convergence, and accuracy under different memory requirements. These substantially change the questions investigated beyond aggregate benchmark performance.

E5.justification: v1 gives no empirical run counts or confidence-interval procedure. v2 Appendix A reports averages over 20 randomized hyperparameter trials and 50 inverse-optimization runs, with 95% confidence intervals assuming normally distributed errors for the latter. These are newly reported statistical practices; an increase in runs for the retained experiment is not established.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the hyperparameter loss curves, adds training-loss and basis-size results, and removes the temperature heatmap outcomes. Its new inverse study reports a gap within 3% at five basis functions, with comparable stocBiO accuracy at 50 subproblems. Changed configurations and incompletely matched settings prevent interpreting the replacement curves as cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Assumption 3.1 removes global Lipschitz continuity of g. Definition 3.4 and Proposition 4.2 replace the earlier approximation condition and transfer bound with squared-error versions using gradient smoothness. Appendix C also introduces a lower-solution Lipschitz lemma and replaces the uniform lower-gradient variance argument with a bound requiring bounded distance from W to W*. These substantially revise the assumptions and proofs.

C1.justification: The central joint-sampling reduction and near-optimal O-tilde(epsilon^-3) complexity claims remain. v2 broadens the empirical contribution from hyperparameter optimization to inverse optimization and adds explicit sample-efficiency and memory-saving claims in the abstract, contributions, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving shared updates across neighboring contexts, redundant partition-wise computation, and basis-dependent saturation, plus conditions explaining excluded solvers' difficulties in Appendix A. It removes v1's explicit low-/high-temperature accuracy tradeoff and discussion of conservative complexity bounds. The mechanism and applicability discussion is substantially revised.

D1.justification: v2 Section 5 and Appendix A disclose the MNIST 19,000/1,000 split, classifier and loss, temperature distribution, batch size, regularization, tuning grids, inverse-Hessian estimator settings, hardware/runtime, and synthetic-data generation. v1 lacks an experimental-details appendix and most corresponding information. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to every retained setting.

R1.justification: The same three research areas organize related work. v2 adds references supporting inverse optimization, traffic assignment, MNIST, and EPOCH-GD, while removing the comparison with Alessandri et al.'s finite-dimensional approximation and the Finn et al. reference. These are focused citation and positioning changes within the retained framing.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v1's separate results and theoretical-analysis sections are integrated into v2 Section 4; experimental subsections and Appendix A are introduced, and existing proofs are reorganized into Appendices B–E. Feature-map terminology and notation are also revised throughout.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column to single-column layout. v1's reduction diagram and temperature heatmaps are removed, its runtime plot is replaced by paired training/validation epoch plots, and v2 adds a three-panel inverse-optimization figure with error bars. Appendix regularity tables are also restructured.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's sparsely documented demonstration, v2's additional application, basis analyses, and experimental specifications make the empirical work easier to assess and reproduce. These gains are tempered by removal of direct CSBO baselines and temperature diagnostics. The theoretical relaxation is also incompletely incorporated: Appendix D still invokes the L_g,0 Lipschitz bound removed from the assumptions. The evidence therefore supports a limited net quality improvement.
